program_name: Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism (IMaST / IMAST) — Laurea Magistrale (Master's Degree). Italian/administrative course code [A215]. Also referred to on the department site as 'Master in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism'.
teaching_language: English — fully English-taught. Department page: 'The course is taught entirely in English in the city of Olbia - 100 Km from Sassari.' The uniss.it course record lists 'Lingua del corso: Inglese' and 'Lingua/e ufficiali di insegnamento e di accertamento della preparazione: INGLESE'. There is no Italian-language curriculum or partially-English track; the master's thesis must also be written in English ('La tesi di laurea magistrale redatta in lingua inglese'). Note: for the sister programme 'Master in Economics' at the same department the entry interview is in Italian, but for IMAST the whole process and teaching is in English.
campus: Olbia (Sardinia) — NOT Sassari city. Teaching is delivered on the first floor of the Olbia Costa Smeralda Airport building, approximately 100 km from Sassari. The uniss.it course record states the location simply as 'OLBIA'. The administering department (DiSEA — Dipartimento di Scienze Economiche e Aziendali) has its administrative seat in Sassari (Via Muroni 25, 07100 Sassari), but all lectures take place in Olbia and in-person attendance is expected. Accommodation for Olbia-based students is signposted via Cool & Young Residence (Olbia).
degree_class: LM-77 — Scienze economico-aziendali (Economics and Business Administration). The uniss.it course record shows the class as '[LM-77-R] Scienze economico-aziendali' (R = reformed class code).
admission_type: Open access (no numerus clausus / no ranked competition) BUT with a compulsory admission check before enrolment. The uniss.it course record states 'Tipologia di accesso: Libero' (free/open access). However, admission is conditional on verification of curricular requirements and, where those are not evidenced, on passing a personal-preparation assessment: 'L'ammissione al Corso di Laurea Magistrale è subordinata alla certificazione del possesso dei requisiti curriculari predeterminati, o in assenza, al superamento di una verifica dell'adeguatezza della personale preparazione da parte di una apposita Commissione.' In practice this means: (a) Italian/EU-degree candidates go through an access interview (colloquio di accesso) held in fixed rounds; (b) international/visa-requiring candidates go through a formal eligibility screening plus a multiple-choice entry test and an English test in a fixed January–March application window. There is no published local quota (posti riservati) specific to IMAST — the university's general non-EU page notes that visa-requiring students are enrolled 'within the quota of places reserved for each study program according to the type of access provided (national or local programmed access)', which does not bite for an 'accesso libero' programme; EU citizens and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy 'access university courses without quota limitations'. [uncertain: absence of an IMAST-specific non-EU numeric cap is inferred from the 'accesso libero' classification; no explicit cap or explicit 'no cap' statement for IMAST was found on the official pages]
academic_requirements:
ACCEPTED DEGREES: A Bachelor's degree (or equivalent foreign qualification). Direct curricular fit is assumed for Italian classes ex D.M. 270/04 L-18 (Scienze dell'economia e della gestione aziendale) and L-33 (Scienze economiche), or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad.

CREDIT (ECTS/CFU) REQUIREMENT: Candidates from other degree classes must document the equivalent of at least 40 CFU/ECTS across the following Italian scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD): economic area SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/12; economic-managerial area SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/10; mathematical-quantitative area SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/04, SECS-S/05, SECS-S/06; legal area IUS/01, IUS/04, IUS/05, IUS/06, IUS/09. For candidates holding a foreign degree the curricular check is made by reference to the actual content of the courses taken ('la verifica curriculare farà riferimento ai contenuti delle specifiche attività didattiche'), not to the Italian SSD codes literally.

SUBSTANTIVE COMPETENCES ASSESSED: analysis of the company's economic and financial performance; ability to understand the environmental/business context from an economic and financial perspective; quantitative problem-solving skills; knowledge of basic descriptive-statistics techniques; ability to analyse economic and business problems. The department publishes a detailed 'Basic knowledge requirements' syllabus covering (i) business administration (systemic approach to the firm, organisational structure, firm/environment relationship and stakeholder theory, conditions of sustainable profitability, purpose and structure of financial statements, financial performance analysis); (ii) quantitative topics (frequency distributions and their graphical representation, summary statistics of central tendency/shape/dispersion, elements of probability theory; spreadsheet skills helpful; reference text Newbold, Carlson & Thorne, 'Statistics for Business and Economics'); (iii) economics (opportunity cost, trade-offs, comparative advantage, marginal thinking, incentives, graphs and slopes, gains from trade, supply/demand/elasticity, government policies, externalities, public goods and common resources, environmental policy, firms in competitive markets, macro basics — GDP and its components, real vs nominal GDP; reference text Mankiw, 'Essentials of Economics', 6th ed. onwards); (iv) law (fundamentals of public and private law, transport law institutions, elements of travel and tourism law).

ADMISSION-DETERMINING STRUCTURE: For international (visa-requiring) applicants the decisive step is a multiple-choice test on business, quantitative, economic and legal topics, PLUS a separate written multiple-choice English test; an interview may substitute for the multiple-choice academic test. For Italian-degree holders who lack the required 40 CFU in the listed SSDs, the decisive step is the access interview (colloquio di accesso) on the same 'basic knowledge' syllabus.

DOUBLE DEGREE STRUCTURE (affects year 2): 'A group of selected students of the Master in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism of the University of Sassari will be able to achieve the double degree in Business Administration in International Hospitality and Tourism proposed by the Babeș-Bolyai University of Cluj-Napoca, with student exchange during the second year of study (semester 3 and semester 4) (Renewed in 2024) (validity 2020/21-2027/28).' The double degree is therefore a competitive, selection-based option within the programme (not automatic on admission) and moves semesters 3 and 4 to Cluj-Napoca, Romania. Selection criteria and the number of double-degree places are not published on the official course pages. [uncertain: double-degree selection procedure and number of places]

CURRICULUM CONTEXT: 120 CFU over 2 years. Year 1: Economics of Sustainable Tourism (12), Strategic Management and Governance for Tourism Companies (12), International Tourism Marketing (6), Legal Models for Sustainable Tourism and Mobility LAB (12), Data Analysis and Forecasting Methods for Sustainable Tourism (12), elective (6). Year 2: Natural Capital and Ecosystem Services (6), Innovation Management and Tourism Service Design (12), Equality Sustainability and Well-Being Measurement LAB (6), Financial Instruments Laboratory for Sustainable Tourism (6), two electives (6 each), final exam/thesis (12). Attendance is 'consigliata ma non obbligatoria' (recommended but not compulsory) in the official record, although the department page states students are expected to attend in person in Olbia.
language_requirements:
English at CEFR level B2 is required: 'English at B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages' and, in the official Italian course record, 'è richiesta una padronanza della lingua inglese almeno pari al livello B2 o equivalente'.

HOW IT IS EVIDENCED: UNISS does NOT publish a fixed score table (no IELTS / TOEFL / Cambridge minimum-score list is given anywhere on the official course or department pages). Instead, English proficiency is verified by the university itself: 'A tal fine è previsto l'accertamento delle conoscenze e competenze nella lingua inglese, esonerando gli studenti in possesso di corrispondente certificazione linguistica internazionale' — i.e. an English assessment is administered, and candidates already holding a corresponding recognised international language certificate are exempted from it. For international applicants the assessment takes the concrete form of 'a written multiple-choice English test' delivered as part of the entry test session. Which certificates and which levels qualify for exemption is decided case by case and is not listed publicly. [uncertain: exact list of accepted certificates and minimum scores — no fixed score table published]

Also note that 'English for Business' (6 CFU) is available as an elective inside the programme, and the thesis must be written in English.
application_deadline_eu:
There is no single published application deadline for EU/Italian-qualification candidates; admission runs through FIXED ACCESS-INTERVIEW ROUNDS, and enrolment (immatricolazione) is completed after passing the round.

2026/2027 ROUNDS (currently published, official Italian text): access interviews for Italian students needed in order to enrol for a.y. 26/27 will be held in (1) September 2026, (2) mid/late October 2026, and (3) the second week of January 2027 — 'Si ricorda che i colloquio di accesso per studenti italiani necessari per poter effettuare l'immatricolazione per l'a.a. 26/27 si terranno a settembre 2026, a metà/fine ottobre 2026 e nella seconda settimana di gennaio 2027.' Exact calendar days for these three 2026/27 rounds have not been published; only the month/period is given. [uncertain: exact days of the three 2026/27 interview rounds]

2025/2026 ROUNDS (previous year, for comparison, from the same page before the September 2026 update): September 2025, mid/late October 2025, and the second week of January 2026.

CONDITIONAL / LATE ENROLMENT: The existence of a January round (second week of January 2027) is what allows candidates who have not yet completed their Bachelor's degree at the September/October round to be admitted later in the academic year — the January round is the last opportunity to enrol for that academic year. A formal 'conditional enrolment' (immatricolazione sotto condizione) rule with an explicit degree-completion date (e.g. 31 December) is not stated on the IMAST course or department pages; the operative constraint published is that the entry procedure must be completed at one of the three rounds and enrolment finalised by mid-January. [uncertain: whether a formal conditional-enrolment mechanism with a separate degree-completion deadline exists for EU candidates — not stated on the official IMAST pages]

PRACTICAL NOTE: the documentation required for the interview must be submitted at least one week in advance — 'The link for the interview will be sent only to who give all documentation required one week before the interview.'

entry_exam_or_test:
YES — there is a compulsory admission assessment, but its format differs by candidate profile, and BOTH the academic component and the English component are genuinely admission-determining for international candidates (neither is purely diagnostic).

A) INTERNATIONAL / VISA-REQUIRING CANDIDATES — 'ENTRY TEST', two components:
   1. An academic component: a MULTIPLE-CHOICE TEST on business, quantitative, economic and legal topics (the 'Basic knowledge required' syllabus), OR an interview in its place — 'Participation in the entrance test, which consists of multiple-choice test (or in an interview) to verify the candidate's requirements and personal preparation'. For IMAST specifically: 'To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism, you must pass a multiple-choice test on business, quantitative, economic and legal topics (basic knowledge required).' This is pass/fail and gates admission.
   2. A WRITTEN MULTIPLE-CHOICE ENGLISH TEST, taken in the same session.
   MODE: remote — 'The entry test is likely to be conducted remotely.' A link is sent to candidates who have supplied all documentation one week in advance. (The precise platform is not named on the official pages; the process is described as an online/remote test with a link sent by the department. [uncertain: exact platform, e.g. Microsoft Teams])
   DATES for 2026/27: all tests and interviews in MARCH and APRIL 2026, with the LAST test in APRIL 2026 (booking by 31 March 2026). No further international entry tests for 2026/27 after 1 April 2026.

B) ITALIAN / EU-QUALIFICATION CANDIDATES — 'COLLOQUIO DI ACCESSO' (access interview):
   An interview before enrolment to verify curricular requirements and personal preparation — 'An interview will be carried out before enrollment in order to verify the position of the candidate's requirements and personal preparation.' Formally, this personal-preparation check is only triggered where the predetermined curricular requirements (the 40 CFU across the listed SSDs) are not certified: 'L'ammissione al Corso di Laurea Magistrale è subordinata alla certificazione del possesso dei requisiti curriculari predeterminati, o in assenza, al superamento di una verifica dell'adeguatezza della personale preparazione da parte di una apposita Commissione.' The interview content is the published 'Basic knowledge requirements' syllabus.
   ROUNDS for 2026/27 (three): September 2026; mid/late October 2026; second week of January 2027.
   ROUNDS for 2025/26 (three, previous year): September 2025; mid/late October 2025; second week of January 2026.

C) ENGLISH ASSESSMENT (all candidates): an English knowledge and competence assessment is administered, with exemption for holders of a corresponding recognised international language certificate.

No TOLC, no SAT and no national admission test applies to this programme.

tuition_or_fees_link:
Programme-level statement (DiSEA): 'Fees are up to a maximum of 1620,00 € (which can be reduced on the basis of the fulfilment of certain conditions)'. Fee page: https://www.uniss.it/en/teaching/student-services/guide-studenti/tuition-fees-and-isee (Italian equivalent under uniss.it 'Guide per studenti / Tasse e ISEE').

STRUCTURE — income-based (ISEE), not a flat figure. The single all-inclusive enrolment contribution is computed with the formula Fee = a + ((ISEE - b) * c) on these brackets (Table A, students meeting merit and income requirements): ISEE 0–22,000 € → 0 €; 22,000.01–30,000 € → minimum 0, base 22,000, coefficient 0.06; 30,000.01–70,000 € → minimum 1,050.00 €, base 30,000, coefficient 0.0175; over 70,000.01 € → 1,750.00 €. A 'No Tax Area' full exemption applies under Law 232/2016 to students meeting the income and merit requirements. Partial reductions (Table A1) apply as: ISEE 22,000–24,000 → 80% reduction; 24,000–26,000 → 50%; 26,000–28,000 → 25%; 28,000–30,000 → 10%. If the ISEE/DSU declaration is not completed or data retrieval is not authorised, the student is automatically placed in the HIGHEST income bracket and pays the maximum amount.

FOREIGN STUDENTS RESIDING ABROAD — special regime: 'Foreign students residing abroad are fully exempt from paying the single registration fee for the first year of enrolment.' From the second year (within the normal course duration) they pay a single registration fee based on the income bracket of their country of residence, parameterised to GDP per capita (PPP) per the IMF: Bracket 1 = €700.00; Bracket 2 = €500.00; Bracket 3 = €400.00; Bracket 4 = €300.00. The DiSEA page confirms this in plain terms: 'Normally, foreign students do not pay any fees for the first year, but they have to pay the "bollo" of 16 € and the "regional tax" of 140 €. For the second year, international students pay a fee depending on their country of residence.' Fees are paid via PagoPA. The department cautions that the 'Student Guide – Guida carriere studenti' containing fee amounts is only updated each July, so the amount for the upcoming academic year is not known in advance.

SCHOLARSHIPS — UNISS OFFERS NONE OF ITS OWN: 'The University of Sassari does not have any scholarships (any financial aid, including grants and bursaries) for international students.' Applicants are redirected to two external schemes: (1) ERSU Sassari (regional right-to-study agency, https://ersusassari.it/it/) — deadline for the current cycle: 7 September 2026, 1:00 PM Italian time; (2) MAECI — Italian Government grants for foreign and Italian citizens living abroad (https://www.esteri.it/en/opportunita/borse-di-studio/per-cittadini-stranieri/) — deadline 2:00 p.m. CET of 26 March 2026. (For the previous cycle the corresponding deadlines were ERSU 8 September 2025 and MAECI 16 May 2025.) Accommodation is signposted separately via Cool & Young Residence in Olbia (previously the department listed A.L.M.A. s.r.l. / Geovillage accommodation in Olbia, ~36 m² double rooms with optional single use, common kitchen/co-working/laundry, cleaning, utilities and Wi-Fi, 250 m from the Geovillage ASPO bus stop; contact hospitality@salima.org).

ACCESS METHOD — BOT PROTECTION: The live uniss.it and disea.uniss.it sites are behind AWS WAF / a human-verification (CAPTCHA) challenge and returned HTTP 405 to direct fetches; a browser attempt landed on a 'Human Verification' interstitial, which was not bypassed. All content above was therefore read through Internet Archive Wayback Machine captures of the official pages. Captures used: (a) fresh captures requested on 5 September 2026 — https://web.archive.org/web/20260905163842/https://www.disea.uniss.it/it/i-nostri-corsi/laurea-magistrale-innovation-management-sustainable-tourism-imast , https://web.archive.org/web/20260905164028/https://www.disea.uniss.it/it/node/159 , https://web.archive.org/web/20260905164103/https://www.disea.uniss.it/it/node/160 ; (b) https://web.archive.org/web/20260609144836/https://www.uniss.it/it/didattica/offerta-formativa/lauree-magistrali/innovation-management-sustainable-tourism (9 June 2026); (c) https://web.archive.org/web/20260411114719/... (11 April 2026, prior version of the IMAST page, showing the 2025/26 rounds); (d) https://web.archive.org/web/20260311221056/https://www.uniss.it/en/teaching/student-services/guide-studenti/tuition-fees-and-isee (11 March 2026); (e) https://web.archive.org/web/20260306173842/https://www.uniss.it/en/teaching/student-services/guide-studenti/enrollment-non-eu-students (6 March 2026). No third-party aggregator was used as a source.

CAMPUS: Confirmed as OLBIA, inside the Olbia Costa Smeralda Airport building (first floor), ~100 km from Sassari — NOT Sassari city. The DiSEA department's administrative address (Via Muroni 25, Sassari) appears in page footers and must not be mistaken for the teaching location.

DOUBLE DEGREE: The Babeș-Bolyai University (Cluj-Napoca, Romania) double degree in 'Business Administration in International Hospitality and Tourism' is confirmed, with semesters 3 and 4 spent abroad, agreement renewed in 2024, validity 2020/21–2027/28. It applies only to 'a group of selected students' — it is an in-programme selection, not automatic on admission. The selection criteria, application procedure and number of places are NOT published on the official pages, and the agreement's stated validity ends with 2027/28, so continuation beyond that year is unconfirmed.

EXACT INTERVIEW DATES: The 2026/27 access interviews are given only as month/period (September 2026; mid/late October 2026; second week of January 2027) — no exact calendar days are published for 2026/27. Specific day-level dates that circulate for 2025/26 (e.g. 8 and 11 September 2025, 29–30 October 2025, 9 January 2026) were NOT found in this form on the official uniss.it / disea.uniss.it pages; the official page states only the months for that year too. Candidates must contact bpes@uniss.it or didatticadisea@uniss.it for exact dates.

LANGUAGE EVIDENCE: There is NO fixed IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge score table published by UNISS for this programme. B2 is the stated level; proof is either an accepted international certificate (which exempts the candidate from the university's own English assessment) or passing the written multiple-choice English test in the entry-test session. Which certificates qualify, and at what score, is not published.

ADMISSION TYPE NUANCE: The official record classifies access as 'Libero' (open access), yet passing the entry test / access interview is a hard precondition for enrolment. This is best described as 'open access with a compulsory pass/fail admission assessment', not as a ranked competitive selection. No IMAST-specific numeric quota for non-EU visa students was found on any official page; the absence is consistent with 'accesso libero' but is not explicitly stated for this programme.

EXAM PLATFORM: The entry test is described as 'likely to be conducted remotely' with a link sent by email, but no platform (e.g. Microsoft Teams, Zoom) is named on the official pages.

CONDITIONAL ENROLMENT: No formal 'immatricolazione con riserva' rule with an explicit degree-completion cut-off date (e.g. 31 December) is published on the IMAST or DiSEA pages. The operative published constraints are the three interview rounds (last one in the second week of January 2027) and, for visa students, enrolment by 15 January. Any claim of a 31 December degree-completion rule should be verified directly with the department.

CONTENT CHANGED BETWEEN VERSIONS: Accommodation guidance changed from A.L.M.A. s.r.l. / Geovillage (2025/26 version) to Cool & Young Residence (2026/27 version); the ERSU deadline moved from 8 September 2025 to 7 September 2026 (1 PM Italian time) and MAECI from 16 May 2025 to 26 March 2026. The fee ceiling statement (max €1,620) and the 'no UNISS scholarships for international students' statement are unchanged across both versions.
